claims.text: The target alloy is nominally equiatomic Nb20Ta20Zr20Mo20W20 with trace boron and carbon additions.
The alloy will be fabricated by Laser Powder Bed Fusion followed by solution annealing at 1400°C for 2 hours and aging at 900°C for 10 hours.
The proposed treatment will produce a dual-phase microstructure containing a BCC matrix and Laves-phase precipitates.
The Laves-phase precipitates will be coherent with the BCC matrix.
The Laves precipitates will have a C14 or C15 structure.
Adding 0.5 at.% B and 0.2 at.% C during powder synthesis will cause boron and carbon to segregate to BCC grain boundaries.
Rapid solidification during LPBF suppresses the formation of brittle topologically close-packed phases.
Rapid solidification during LPBF refines the grain size.
Aging at 900°C promotes nucleation of coherent Laves-phase precipitates.
The Laves-phase precipitates impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation hardening.
The coherent Laves-phase precipitates can strengthen the alloy without causing significant embrittlement.
Boron and carbon segregation strengthens grain-boundary cohesion.
Boron and carbon segregation prevents the formation of brittle interstitial-rich phases such as oxides or nitrides.
Interstitial-rich oxides or nitrides typically cause cleavage fracture in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The processed alloy will exhibit a yield strength greater than 800 MPa at 1000°C.
The processed alloy will exhibit tensile ductility greater than 10% at room temperature.
The proposed alloy will significantly outperform conventionally cast or unoptimized LPBF versions of the same composition.
Standard LPBF-fabricated Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W alloys without B/C additions or aging typically have near-zero room-temperature ductility.
Standard LPBF-fabricated Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W alloys rapidly lose strength above 800°C because of grain-boundary sliding and TCP-phase formation.
Excessive B/C segregation could form brittle grain-boundary borides or carbides and reverse the anticipated ductility improvement.
